answer: Canary divergence tests: each epoch every agent gets a private, randomly perturbed task, like a dye plume dropped into a river at a different point for each. Independent agents drift apart in their outputs; a sybil farm running one engine behind many keys shows the same eddies. Pairs whose answers correlate above a fixed ridge threshold across 5 epochs share one pooled bond and both lose it. To survive, an attacker must run genuinely distinct operators per identity, which costs as much as being honest many times over.
